name: Whale Sanctuary of El Vizcaíno
blurb: Gray whale nurseries, eelgrass lagoons and a desert of pronghorn and coyotes.

tip.title: Thin the eelgrass
tip.text: Eelgrass feeds geese, turtles and seafloor amphipods. Set Eelgrass to -80% and watch the amphipods that gray whales eat, then the whales and killer whales.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Drifting algae that form the base of the open-water food chain. Small plankton-eating fish feed on them.
Underwater meadows in sheltered coastal waters. They are grazed by geese and feed small animals when leaves break loose and decay.

nodes.name: Seafloor amphipods
nodes.desc: Small crustaceans that live in sediment and on seaweed. Gray whales feed mainly on bottom-dwelling crustaceans like these.
A schooling fish that feeds on plankton. It is food for sea lions and fish-eating birds.
A grazing sea turtle that feeds on seagrass and algae. Marine turtles breed in the reserve lagoons.
The Baja California form of pronghorn, a rare subspecies. Pronghorn eat forbs, shrubs, grasses and cacti.
A desert hare that eats shrubs and grasses. It is a common food for coyotes in GloBI records.
A seed-eating rodent that rarely drinks, getting water from its food. Snakes, owls and coyotes prey on it.
A coastal seal that breeds and rests on Pacific shores and islands. It feeds mainly on fish and squid.
A fish-eating raptor that hunts along coasts and lagoons. The reserve is home to resident and migratory ospreys.
A top marine predator. Orcas are a main predator of gray whale calves and also hunt seals and sea lions.
The top land predator in these records. It eats rodents, hares and pronghorn fawns, and scavenges carcasses.
Strong year-round sun powers desert shrubs and shallow-water meadows alike.
This is a very dry region. Many desert animals get water from succulents and their food.
Break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the sand and the sea.
